topics: 🔢 Oved-edom's Blessing — how eight sons and nine women add up to sixty-two
⏳ Forcing the Moment — Rabbi Avin HaLevi: the hour pushes aside whoever pushes it
⛰️ Sinai vs. Uprooter of Mountains — Rabba and Rav Yosef, and who should head the yeshiva
🪵 The God of Jacob and the Beam — why the verse names Jacob alone
👋 'Go to Peace' vs. 'Go in Peace' — the right farewell for the living and for the dead
🕊️ Scholars Increase Peace — 'your children' become 'your builders'; the tractate's conclusion

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Closing Amud of Berakhot
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 64a
overview.hebrewSource: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מַרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם — אַל תִּקְרֵי ״בָּנָיִךְ״ אֶלָּא ״בּוֹנָיִךְ״
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The final amud of Berakhot finishes the count of Oved-edom's blessing — sixty-two descendants for having honored the ark — and then gathers a set of teachings from Rabbi Avin HaLevi: one who forces the hour is pushed aside by it, illustrated by Rav Yosef's refusal to head the yeshiva ahead of Rabba; why Psalm 20 invokes 'the God of Jacob'; a meal with a Torah scholar is like basking in the Shekhina; and the precise wording of a farewell. Rabbi Levi bar Ḥiyya praises going straight from synagogue to study hall, Rav says scholars have no rest in either world, and the tractate closes with Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina: Torah scholars increase peace in the world. הדרן עלך הרואה וסליקא לה מסכת ברכות.

slides.title: 🔢 Counting Oved-edom's Blessing
slides.subtitle: The Gemara finishes the a fortiori from the end of 63b: what exactly was the blessing?

nodes.content: ❓ 'The Lord blessed the house of Oved-edom because of the ark' — what was the blessing?
👩‍👧 Rav Yehuda bar Zevida: Ḥamot and her eight daughters-in-law, each bearing six in a single womb
📜 Proof: 'Peulletai the eighth… for God blessed him' (I Chron. 26:4–5) — the eight sons are the blessing; 'sixty-two of Oved-edom' (I Chron. 26:8)

callout.label: The point:
callout.text: If sweeping and sprinkling before an ark that neither ate nor drank earned this, how much more so hosting and feeding a Torah scholar.

slides.title: ⛰️ Sinai or Uprooter of Mountains?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Avin HaLevi's rule about the hour, proved from Rabba and Rav Yosef

lines.speaker: R' Avin HaLevi
lines.text: כׇּל הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה — שָׁעָה דּוֹחַקְתּוֹ. Whoever forces the moment, the moment forces him aside; whoever yields to the moment, the moment yields to him.

lines.speaker: The case
lines.text: Rav Yosef was Sinai — vastly learned in the sources. Rabba was an uprooter of mountains — razor sharp. One of them had to be chosen as head of the yeshiva.

lines.speaker: Babylonia
lines.text: They sent to Eretz Yisrael: Sinai or uprooter of mountains — which takes precedence?

lines.speaker: Eretz Yisrael
lines.text: Sinai takes precedence, for everyone needs the owner of the wheat (מָרֵי חִטַּיָּא).

lines.speaker: Rav Yosef
lines.text: Still he declined — the Chaldean astrologers had told him: 'You will reign for two years.'

lines.speaker: Outcome
lines.text: Rabba presided twenty-two years; afterwards Rav Yosef presided two and a half years. In all Rabba's years, Rav Yosef did not even summon a bloodletter to his house — he assumed no airs of authority.

callout.label: Lesson:
callout.text: Rav Yosef relinquished the opportunity and still ultimately received what was destined for him.

slides.title: 🪵 More From Rabbi Avin HaLevi
slides.subtitle: Three further teachings and their verses
rows: Why 'the God of Jacob' and not of Abraham and Isaac?
'The Lord will answer you on the day of distress; the name of the God of Jacob set you on high' (Ps. 20:2)
The owner of the beam should go in with its thick end — Jacob, who fathered the nation, must carry its heaviest load and keep praying for his children
A meal with a Torah scholar present
'Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God' (Ex. 18:12)
They ate before Moses, not literally before God — so one who enjoys such a meal is as if he enjoyed the radiance of the Shekhina
Taking leave of the living: say לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם, 'go to peace'
Never לֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם, 'go in peace', to the living
David to Absalom, 'Go in peace' (II Sam. 15:9)
Taking leave of the dead: say 'go in peace'
'You shall come to your fathers in peace' (Gen. 15:15)
The reverse of the farewell for the living

slides.title: 🏃 From Strength to Strength
slides.subtitle: Two readings of Psalms 84:8 — and what Torah scholars are and are not granted

steps.content: 1️⃣ R' Levi bar Ḥiyya: one who leaves the synagogue and enters the study hall to engage in Torah merits to receive the Divine Presence
2️⃣ Source: יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל יֵרָאֶה אֶל אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן — 'They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion' (Ps. 84:8)
3️⃣ R' Ḥiyya bar Ashi in the name of Rav: the same verse teaches that Torah scholars have no rest, neither in this world nor in the World-to-Come
4️⃣ Why? Because in both worlds they are always going 'from strength to strength' — constant ascent, never standing still

callout.label: Connection:
callout.text: Prayer leads into study, and study never ends — the daf's build-up to the tractate's closing praise of scholars.

slides.title: 🕊️ Torah Scholars Increase Peace in the World
slides.subtitle: The final teaching of Masechet Berakhot
slides.hebrewSource: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מַרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכׇל בָּנַיִךְ לִמּוּדֵי ה׳ וְרַב שְׁלוֹם בָּנָיִךְ״ — אַל תִּקְרֵי ״בָּנָיִךְ״ אֶלָּא ״בּוֹנָיִךְ״
slides.label: Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina:
slides.text: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it says, 'And all your children shall be taught of the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children' (Isaiah 54:13). Do not read banayikh, your children, but bonayikh, your builders — scholars are the builders of their generation's peace. The Gemara strings together four more verses of peace: 'Those who love Your Torah have great peace; there is no stumbling block for them' (Ps. 119:165); 'May there be peace within your walls, prosperity within your palaces' (Ps. 122:7); 'For the sake of my brothers and friends I shall say: Peace be within you; for the sake of the House of the Lord our God I will seek your good' (Ps. 122:8–9); 'May the Lord give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace' (Ps. 29:11). With that, the tractate ends: הדרן עלך הרואה וסליקא לה מסכת ברכות.

callout.label: Siyum:
callout.text: Berakhot began with the evening Shema — accepting the yoke of Heaven — and closes with the scholars who, by learning, build peace.

summary.principle: Honor for Torah and its scholars brings blessing; do not force the hour, for what is destined arrives in its time; and those who learn Torah are the builders of peace in the world.

flowSteps.content: 🔢 Oved-edom honored the ark → 62 descendants (8 sons + 9 women × 6)
⏳ R' Avin HaLevi: force the hour and it pushes you aside; yield and it yields to you — Rav Yosef (Sinai) declined, served two and a half years after Rabba's twenty-two
🪵 God of Jacob = carry the beam's thick end; a meal with a scholar = radiance of the Shekhina; 'go to peace' for the living, 'go in peace' for the dead

columns.content: 🏃 Synagogue → study hall: receive the Divine Presence (Ps. 84:8)
🏃 Rav: scholars have no rest in this world or the next — always 'strength to strength'

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Torah scholars increase peace in the world — 'not your children but your builders' (Isaiah 54:13). Hadran alakh HaRo'eh, and Masechet Berakhot is complete.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara arrive at sixty-two descendants for Oved-edom?
o: Eight sons each had seven sons
Nine women each bore six sons (54), plus the original eight sons
Ḥamot bore sixty-two children over her lifetime
Each of his eight sons had eight children, minus two
quiz.e: Ḥamot and her eight daughters-in-law — nine women — each bore six in a single womb, giving 54; adding the eight original sons of Oved-edom yields the 'sixty-two' of I Chronicles 26:8.

quiz.q: When Babylonia asked whether 'Sinai' or 'one who uproots mountains' should take precedence, what did the Sages of Eretz Yisrael answer, and why?
o: The uprooter of mountains, because sharpness produces new rulings
Sinai, because everyone needs the owner of the wheat — the master of the sources
Both should serve jointly
Neither; the elder of the two should serve
quiz.e: They answered that Sinai takes precedence, 'for everyone needs the owner of the wheat' (מָרֵי חִטַּיָּא). Even so, Rav Yosef declined because astrologers had told him he would reign only two years.

quiz.q: Why did Rav Yosef not even call a bloodletter to his house during the years Rabba headed the yeshiva?
o: He was too poor to pay one
He did not want to assume even the slightest air of authority while Rabba presided
Bloodletting was forbidden to the head of a yeshiva
Rabba had forbidden it as a decree
quiz.e: The Gemara relates this to show that Rav Yosef, having yielded the position, took on no trappings of authority at all — he went to the bloodletter rather than have him come.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Avin HaLevi, what should one say when taking leave of a living friend, and what is the proof?
o: 'Go in peace' — as David said to Absalom
'Go to peace' — as Jethro said to Moses, who then went up and succeeded
'Come in peace' — as God told Abraham
'Peace be upon you' — as Boaz greeted the harvesters
quiz.e: One says lekh le-shalom, 'go to peace', like Jethro to Moses (Ex. 4:18), who succeeded. 'Go in peace' (be-shalom) is what David told Absalom, who was hanged — and is the wording reserved for the dead (Gen. 15:15).

quiz.q: What homiletic reading supports the tractate's closing statement that Torah scholars increase peace in the world?
o: Read 'your children' (banayikh) as 'your builders' (bonayikh) in Isaiah 54:13
Read 'peace' (shalom) as 'wholeness' (shalem)
Read 'taught of the Lord' as 'judges of the Lord'
Read 'from strength to strength' as 'from peace to peace'
quiz.e: Rabbi Elazar in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina cites 'all your children shall be taught of the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children', and the Sages read banayikh as bonayikh — scholars are the builders of peace.
